claims.statement: MelodyDatabase is the single Room database (file `melody.db`, version 11, `exportSchema = true`) exposing one DAO (`MelodyDao`); `DatabaseModule` builds it as a Hilt `@Singleton` via `Room.databaseBuilder` with all migrations v1→v11 registered by `addMigrations(*MelodyMigrations.ALL)`.

Room v11 contains exactly 14 entity tables: songs (library master with unique `uri` index), playlists, playlist_song_cross_ref (order-preserving many-to-many), play_stats, playback_events (per-session rows for day/week/month aggregation), quick_skip_songs, quick_skip_short_play_counts, song_group_overrides, migration_state, artists, albums, song_artist_cross_ref, song_emotions (per-window V/A curve plus user calibration fields), and word_preferences (emotion word listen-preference tallies).

Room entities declare no foreign-key constraints; all relationships (playlist↔song, song↔artist/album, songId-keyed stat rows) are logical and maintained by repository code — `MelodyDao.syncLibraryCatalog` rebuilds artist/album catalogs, song-artist refs, and the `songs.albumId` backfill idempotently, then deletes orphans.

MusicRepository persists the library as asynchronous full-table snapshots: changes are queued on a single-threaded IO scope (`Dispatchers.IO.limitedParallelism(1)`) that guarantees later snapshots supersede earlier ones, and `RoomMusicLibraryDataSource.persistSongs/persistPlaylists` replace whole tables inside `@Transaction` methods `replaceSongs`/`replacePlaylists` so main-thread UI actions never block on disk.

The composite index `(startedAtMs, isEffectivePlay, songId)` on `playback_events` covers all time-range aggregation queries (total duration, distinct songs, per-day durations, effective-play song TOP chart); migration 7→8 creates it with a `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` so devices that ran the historical v5→v6 single-column-index migration stay compatible, while the v5→v6 migration now creates no index (matching v6's exported schema).

The mandatory Room schema-change workflow is: change entity/DAO → bump `MelodyDatabase` version (currently 11 → next 12) → build `:data` (KSP `room.schemaLocation = $projectDir/schemas`) so the new JSON is exported to `data/schemas/cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.local.MelodyDatabase/` → register a `Migration(N, N+1)` in `MelodyMigrations` and add it to `MelodyMigrations.ALL` (DatabaseModule registers the array via `addMigrations(*MelodyMigrations.ALL)`) → add a focused unit test for migrations with complex data movement; existing schema JSON files are immutable snapshots and must never be edited.

`verifyProductArchitecture` (root `build.gradle.kts`; rule body in `buildSrc` `ProductArchitectureVerification`) machine-enforces persistence invariants: schema v1 must not contain `quick_skip_short_play_counts`, v2 must contain it but not `lrcUri`, v3 must contain `lrcUri`; `MelodyMigrations` must keep `Migration(1, 2)`/`Migration(2, 3)` and `DatabaseModule` must call `addMigrations(*MelodyMigrations.ALL)`; it also walks both backup rule files against the required privacy exclude list.

Migration history v1→v11: 1→2 create `quick_skip_short_play_counts`; 2→3 add `lrcUri`; 3→4 add `album`; 4→5 create `artists`/`albums`/`song_artist_cross_ref` + `songs.albumId`; 5→6 create `playback_events` (no single-column `startedAtMs` index); 6→7 add `durationMs`; 7→8 swap to the composite index; 8→9 create `song_emotions`; 9→10 add `embeddingB64`/`userValence`/`userArousal`/`userTags` to `song_emotions`; 10→11 create `word_preferences` for the explore-play preference tallies.

`SharedPreferencesLegacyJsonMigration` performs the one-shot read-only migration of v1 SharedPreferences JSON into Room: it reads `music_player_prefs` (`songs_json`, `playlists_json`), `play_stats_prefs` (prefixed count/duration keys), and `quick_skip_songs_prefs`, upserts the parsed snapshot via `MelodyDao`, and is the only reason legacy SharedPreferences readers are retained.

Legacy migration idempotency is enforced by a `migration_state` marker row: `migrateIfNeeded()` short-circuits when `MigrationStateEntity("shared_preferences_json_v1", completedAt)` exists, and writes the marker only after the data upserts complete.

`LegacyJsonSnapshotParser` isolates parse failures per JSON block (`runCatching` per section, degrading to empty without blocking the others), deduplicates songs by `uri`, and filters playlist song references to ids that exist among successfully parsed songs; a test locks down that corrupt JSON still migrates stats and writes the completion marker.

The legacy migration trigger point is `MusicRepository.loadPersistedSongs()`, which runs `migrateIfNeeded()` before restoring from Room — after the one-shot migration Room is the single source of truth and legacy JSON is never consulted again.

The `player_settings` DataStore (owned by `PlayerSettingsRepository` via `PlayerSettingsKeys`) persists theme mode/variant (variant defaults to MONO), screen-orientation mode (default SENSOR_AUTO), uniform-random, Bluetooth monitoring, playback notification, lyric font scale, sleep timer end time + play-last-song, daily listening goal, emotion-scan pause, the random-enhance mode (`RANDOM_ENHANCE_MODE`, whose legacy `mood_time_slot_enabled` mirror is written back in the same transaction), and local-music sort mode (default IMPORT_ORDER) + sort ascending (default true); `DataStoreModule` provides it plus the legacy `music_player_prefs` SharedPreferences behind Hilt qualifiers.

Player settings reads carry a legacy SharedPreferences fallback and the write path deletes the legacy key: when DataStore lacks a value the legacy `dark_theme`-style key is consulted (theme additionally falls back through an in-DataStore `dark_theme` boolean before the SharedPreferences key), and an explicit write (e.g. `setThemeMode`) both writes DataStore and removes the legacy key, so legacy values decay with use.

The sleep timer's end timestamp (`sleep_timer_end_at_ms`) and play-last-song flag are persisted so `PlayerSleepTimerCoordinator.restore()` resurrects an unexpired countdown after app restart, resetting expired timers to zero; restore is a suspend `first()` read (no blocking).

`PlaybackStateStore` (in `:player`, implementing both `PlaybackStateStorage` and `PlaybackStateRepository`) owns the `playback_state` DataStore with keys `play_queue_json`, `play_position_ms`, `is_infinite_play`, `infinite_played_ids`, `is_explore_play`, `current_song_id`; it is the process-death recovery snapshot for the Media3 session and is wired through `app/di/PlayerModule`.

Playback snapshot save semantics: an empty session (empty queue, no currentSongId, not infinite play) never writes queue JSON over an existing DataStore snapshot — with an existing snapshot it keeps the queue and updates only currentSongId+position, with no snapshot but a present currentSongId it writes a single-song queue for restore-time correction, and only a fully empty save with no prior snapshot writes nothing. Explicit clearing goes through `clear()`, legacy keys are cleared on write only when DataStore actually changed, and save failures are logged and swallowed so playback control is never interrupted.

`PlaybackStateSnapshotSerializer` encodes the queue as `{songIds, currentIndex, playMode, playOrderIds}` JSON preserving duplicates; decoding filters song ids against the current library, clamps `currentIndex`, repairs the play order against matched ids, and returns null on corrupt JSON or a missing `currentIndex` (a missing `playMode` defaults to `PlayMode.DEFAULT`); infinite-play played ids are likewise filtered to available songs.

Restore is a two-phase decision that removes the controller race: `PlayerPersistenceGraph` lazily builds `PlaybackStateStore`, `PlaybackRestoreCoordinator`, `PlayerPersistenceFacade`, and `PlayerPlaybackStateAutosaver`; `restorePlaybackState()` reads/decodes the snapshot on an IO coroutine while the controller connects, `onControllerReady()` sets `controllerReady`, and both rendezvous in `maybeApplyRestore()` which waits for `controllerReady` and a non-null `pendingRestore` before consulting `hasLiveSession()` — a live session receives only the UI queue shadow backfill (never controller overwrite), while a cold start fully restores UI plus controller queue without autoplay; `PlaybackStateStore.restore` also re-anchors the queue onto the stored `current_song_id`, synthesizing a single-song queue if the song was not in the saved queue.

Snapshot writes have two safety nets: `PlayerPlaybackStateAutosaver` saves every 5 seconds (`DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000L`) on playback position, and `AppMediaSessionService.onDestroy`/`onTaskRemoved` write the final snapshot via the suspend `persistCurrentPlaybackSnapshot` on a process-level `@ApplicationScope` coroutine (ExoPlayer state must be read on the calling thread; only the disk write is async) and settle the playlist resume record in the same coroutine.

`PlaylistResumeDataStore` (the `playlist_resume` DataStore) keeps one `resume_<playlistId>` key holding `{"songId":N,"updatedAtMs":T}` JSON plus a `source_playlist_id` marker for the queue's source playlist; `switchSourcePlaylist` and `recordCurrentSource` must read-and-write inside a single `edit` transaction, otherwise rapid source switching can settle a song onto the wrong playlist.

`PlaylistResumeDataStoreTest` locks down the transactional semantics (switching settles the old source playlist with the current song, same-source switch does not settle, switching to non-playlist source settles then clears, `recordCurrentSource` returns whether a record was made) and that corrupt resume JSON observes as null.

`TimeSlotConfigStore` (the `mood_time_slot` DataStore) stores all mood time-slot configs in the single key `time_slot_configs` as a JSONArray of `{id, name, start, end, tags}` — chosen over Room because the config count is single-digit to low-double-digit; `save` validates via `MoodSlotResolver.validate` (name/tags/zero-length/overlap) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` carrying the conflicting slot's name, rewriting the whole key sorted by start time.

Time-slot config parsing is two-level fault tolerant: an outer `runCatching` degrades a wholly corrupt value to an empty list, while an inner per-entry `runCatching` skips a single corrupted slot (with a warning log) instead of discarding the entire config list.

Runtime consumption of mood time-slot configs and emotion tags is flow-based: `PlayerRuntime.observeMoodSlotCaches()` continuously collects `timeSlotConfigRepository.observeConfigs()`, `songEmotionRepository.observeAll()` (mapped to tag maps), and `wordPreferenceRepository.observeAll()` into `@Volatile` caches at startup, and `PlayerRandomQueueFacade` evaluates the active time-slot / word-preferences on each random draw to filter the candidate pool.

`EmotionFailureStore` (the `emotion_failures` DataStore) persists emotion-analysis failures in one key `emotion_failures` as a JSONObject keyed by songId with `{reason, failedAt, attempts}`; `record` read-modify-writes in one transaction accumulating `attempts` and overwriting `reason`/`failedAt` with the latest, and parsing skips corrupted entries.

`EmotionScanWorker` consumes failure records: songs with `attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS (3)` are excluded from automatic retry so periodic scans do not spin on broken files (manual retry goes through `clearForRetry`, which clears records and re-enqueues), and a successful analysis clears the record via `clear(songId)`.

The periodic emotion scan is scheduled once per app start by `EmotionScanScheduler.schedule` from `MelodyApplication.onCreate`: a unique periodic WorkManager job (`emotion_periodic_scan`, KEEP policy) every 6 hours with charging + battery-not-low constraints and a 30-minute initial delay, ≤40 songs per pass.

Most `:data` persistence repositories expose suspend/`Flow` APIs that `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` the Room query rather than blocking: `SongEmotionsRepository`, `PlayStatsRepository` (with atomic SQL upserts such as `incrementPlayCount`), `QuickSkipSongsRepository`, and `PlayerSettingsRepository` (Flow observation + suspend writes) were refactored (M-5) away from runBlocking(IO) bridges. `runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO)` remains only in `PlaybackStateStore.save`/`restore`/`clear`, which serve the synchronous `PlaybackStateStorage`/`PlaybackStateRepository` contracts consumed by the Media3 session.

Backup/privacy exclusions are a release checklist item: `backup_rules.xml` (`full-backup-content`) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (both `cloud-backup` and `device-transfer` scenarios) must both exclude the legacy SharedPreferences (`music_player_prefs.xml`, `play_stats_prefs.xml`, `quick_skip_songs_prefs.xml`), the full Room family (`melody.db`, `-journal`, `-shm`, `-wal`), all five DataStore files (`player_settings`, `playback_state`, `playlist_resume`, `mood_time_slot`, `emotion_failures` `.preferences_pb`), and the album-art caches; `verifyProductArchitecture` walks a `requiredPrivacyExcludes` subset (legacy prefs, Room family, player_settings/playback_state DataStores, `cache/album_art/`) against both files and fails the build if any entry is missing.

The DataStore-versus-Room selection rule applied in this codebase: only small, non-relational state goes to DataStore — both `TimeSlotConfigStore` and `EmotionFailureStore` explicitly document 'no Room schema change' as the rationale for JSON-in-DataStore storage, while anything relational or aggregate (library, playlists, stats, emotions) lives in Room.

Persistence has a JVM regression floor: `PlaybackStateStoreTest` (round trip, unavailable-song filtering, infinite/explore-play state, empty-session keep semantics, currentSongId correction, legacy fallback + clear-on-save), `PlaybackStateSnapshotSerializerTest` (round trip, corrupt JSON, missing currentIndex, defaults), `SharedPreferencesLegacyJsonMigrationTest`, `PlaylistResumeDataStoreTest`, and `PlayerSettingsRepositoryTest` lock the behaviors this page documents; changes to these paths must keep those tests green.

Dedup persistence flow: `SongRepository.scanDuplicateSongGroups()`/`deduplicateSongs()` (delegated by `SongRepositoryAdapter` to `MusicRepository`, suspend and dispatched to IO) group songs by `SongPathResolver.resolveRealPath(uri)` (normalizing file/MediaStore/SAF URIs to the same on-disk path; unresolvable songs are excluded so normalization failure never causes a false positive), keep the smallest songId per path as the `keep` entry, and `deduplicateSongs` removes duplicates from the library under the write lock (playlist songIds + a full-table `persistSongs`/`persistPlaylists` snapshot) WITHOUT deleting the underlying physical file, then calls `cleanupMissingSongAssociations` to purge orphan records from play_stats, playback_events, quick_skip_songs, quick_skip_short_play_counts, song_emotions, and orphan artists/albums.

`WordPreferencesRepository` is the sole data source of the Room `word_preferences` table (added in v11, 2026-10-20 explore play): each emotion word keyed by `word` holds likeVotes/dislikeVotes/updatedAt; `recordSongOutcome` only accumulates votes (+1 on the matching side, words deduplicated, empty input is a no-op) and never overwrites an affinity, while the domain `WordPreference.kind` (core/model/WordPreference.kt) decisively labels LIKE/DISLIKE/NEUTRAL by vote majority (tie = neutral), so a single skip cannot flip a liked word. Consumer `PlayerRuntime.handleExploreSongSettled` decides via `ExplorePlaybackPolicy.isSkipped` and records `liked = !skipped`; `PlayerRandomQueueFacade` filters candidates by kind.

Emotion analysis runs under `android:largeHeap="true"`, and both `EmotionAnalyzer` and `FfmpegPcmDecoder` share a single adaptive decode memory budget sourced from `EmotionAnalyzer.memoryBudgetForHeap(Runtime.getRuntime().maxMemory())` = (maxHeap − 64MB baseline reservation) clamped to [96MB, 512MB] — 256MB heap → 192MB, 512MB → 448MB. The budget bounds decode buffer + resample output (steady and transient peaks above 64kHz) and decides whether an oversized/high-rate song is reported `TOO_LARGE_FOR_DEVICE` (memory cap hit first) versus `TOO_LONG` (duration cap hit first).
